name: Cerebellar Liponeurocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and radiological diagnostic criteria for cerebellar liponeurocytoma

criteria.description: Presence of neurocytic tumor cells with focal lipomatous differentiation on histopathology
MRI showing a well-circumscribed cerebellar mass with heterogeneous signal intensity including fat components
Positive immunostaining for neuronal markers such as synaptophysin and NeuN
Symptoms consistent with posterior fossa mass effect such as ataxia or headache

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of neurocytic tumor with lipomatous differentiation plus supportive imaging and immunohistochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, radiological, and pathological data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting due to high brain pressure
throwing up from increased intracranial pressure
memory and thinking decline from brain fluid

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to tumor compression

laboratory: Generally normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated cerebellar mass with mixed solid and fatty components
T1-weighted hyperintense areas indicating fat content
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; rare reports of TP53 mutations
other: Histopathology revealing neurocytic cells with lipidized cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for synaptophysin, NeuN, and variable GFAP

distinguishingFeatures: Usually lacks fat components on imaging

redFlags: Severe headache with vomiting and papilledema
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC; 2021.
Kleinschmidt-DeMasters BK, et al. Cerebellar liponeurocytoma: a clinicopathologic study of 10 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2000.
